title: Learning orchestral ranges and stock arrangements in bands
summary: He learned instrument ranges from stock parts, and bands like Johnson's and Fowler's played stocks.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So in what sense do you think you owe ... well, maybe that's a poor way to put it, but -- you might have emulated just the orchestral style of these people by doing this kind of early arranging method; that is, their particular voicings or their particular harmonic style?

Well, I guess I got something from each of them, or something; I don't know. Harmonic style, I guess that was dictated by what I heard, and when I would sit down at the piano and kind of figure out, you know. What I would look at their parts for was for getting the mechanics of, you know, putting things down, properly for the instruments.

And I would look to see how high they would write their first trumpet, or how low they would write the other trumpets, and I had to learn you know, the natural compass of the instruments, and I guess I got that first from looking at these parts and seeing where they would write them, and I'd note, you know, how it sounded there. And usually things that we had been playing or that I had heard, or, you know, something I'd know.

This is a bit of (unintelligible) but how frequently, or if indeed, that it happened very often that, what we would today consider jazz bands would simply play stock arrangements as they were -- as they were published.

Well, I guess it would ... I don't know that it would happen with a great deal of frequency with bands like Charlie Johnson or that ... I don't know; I guess so, though. Because they would always be having arrangements made by members of the band, you know, there were other people who were writing all the time. I don't know. But I do remember playing a number of stock arrangements with the Charlie Johnson orchestra.
But I don't remember playing too many with Fletcher, with the Henderson band. With Fowler, maybe even more. Yes.
